clue.text: Rough for friend on team in a police dept

indicators.note: the run of pieces before it is placed inside the letters from 'a police dept'

parts.note: PD is the American abbreviation for police department

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece 'on' another comes after it

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a cricket or football side
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A puzzling note about a friend joining a squad inside a police department.
explanation.walkthrough: PD is the US abbreviation for police department; in an across clue 'on' places the friend after the team.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough estimate is one that has been worked out only approximately, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: The highest-rated stadium on earth

parts.note: A is the top grade or rating, as in A-list
a ground is a sports stadium

explanation.surface: Boasting about the best-rated sports arena on the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on earth' looks like part of the boast about the world; it is the definition, as a ship stuck on the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that has run onto land or the seabed is stranded, resting on solid ground.

clue.text: Plan to catch one fly

indicators.note: the plan word grips the numeral for one inside itself

parts.note: a plot is a plan or scheme
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A scheme for trapping a single insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like the insect to be caught, but it is the verb, to steer an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly an aircraft is to be at its controls, which is the work of an aviator.

clue.text: Using line of torches, tracked people in pit

indicators.note: the answer is a line of consecutive letters taken from the next words

explanation.surface: Following a line of torches, someone tracked down people hiding in a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'torches, tracked', ignoring the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: The musicians of a theatre band sit in the sunken area before the stage, called the pit.

clue.text: Via road regularly used, finish in southern country

indicators.note: every second letter of the two words is taken
the final letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Directions: take this road and you end up in a southern country.
explanation.walkthrough: Every other letter of 'Via road' gives I, R, A; the end of 'southern' adds N.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a nation of the Middle East, formerly known as Persia.

clue.text: Wrote date with hour to be arranged

indicators.note: the letters of date and hour are to be put into a new order

explanation.surface: A diary note: wrote down a date, with the time still to be arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: DATE plus HOUR is rearranged into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To have written a book or article is to have been its writer, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Dainty female carried by river to the north

indicators.note: the female letter is held inside the river word
in a down clue, going north means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river

explanation.surface: A delicate woman being ferried along a river heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' turns NILE into ELIN, and F goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something small and delicate, like a sprite or fairy, is called this.

clue.text: Stress-free times with beer served up in club

indicators.note: the beer and times pieces go inside the club word

parts.note: a ring is a club or gang, as in a smuggling ring

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: ale is beer
X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: Easy times with a beer handed round at the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses the beer to ELA. 'club' is a group of people, as in a crime ring, not a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is calming and soothing leaves one at ease, free of tension.

clue.text: Street carnival turned camp

indicators.note: the carnival word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a gala is a festive carnival

explanation.surface: A street party that turned into a tent camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses the carnival word. A stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a German prisoner-of-war compound during the Second World War.

clue.text: Resisting shifting clutter covering article

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap round the article
the letters of clutter are moved about

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone who will not move the clutter piled over an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' rearranges CLUTTER into RELUCTT, which covers AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unwilling to do something holds back and is disinclined, putting up resistance.

clue.text: Leave time for craft group

parts.note: to flee is to leave in a hurry

explanation.surface: Taking time off work for a crafts club meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft group' suggests a hobby circle; here craft means boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A navy's collection of ships, or vessels sailing together, is a group of craft.

clue.text: Released bunny, tail end dropped off and on

indicators.note: letters are dropped and kept in turn, so every second one of the next words survives

explanation.surface: A rabbit was set free, its tail end bobbing as it hopped off and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail end' looks like the usual signal for a last letter, but it is just part of the fodder: the even letters of 'bunny tail end' spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfastening a knot or tether sets free whatever was bound, so it means freed.

clue.text: Teacher consuming whiskey following everyone failing

indicators.note: the teacher word takes in the whiskey letter

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
Whiskey is the NATO alphabet word for W
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A teacher who drinks whisky, followed by the whole school failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' is used as a noun, a flaw that brings ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A weakness or failing that leads to someone's ruin is their undoing or collapse.

clue.text: Suspects cook bust mobile

parts.note: to do food is to cook it, as in do the potatoes

indicators.note: mobile means moving, so the letters of bust are shifted

explanation.surface: Police suspect a cook of a raid on a mobile phone ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspects' looks like a plural noun but is a verb; 'mobile' rearranges 'bust' to UBTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect something is to have misgivings or be unsure about it, a verb of uncertainty.

clue.text: Indecent Frenchman's one caught with urgency

parts.note: un is the French for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
haste is urgency or hurry

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's indecent behaviour, caught in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking purity or modesty in sexual matters, the word is a near-synonym of improper or immodest.

clue.text: Desire 12 months at home? No good hiding that

parts.note: a year is twelve months

indicators.note: the no-good letters conceal the at-home word within them

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A year stuck at home, with a longing to hide that it was no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' means the no-good letters enclose 'at home'; 'that' refers back to 'at home'.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong longing or wish for something is a desire, a noun in both cases.

clue.text: It is clear eccentric is genuine

indicators.note: odd or off-centre, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: It is plain that the oddball is the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' looks like a noun, a character; it rearranges IT IS CLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lifelike and true to life seems authentic rather than fake or fanciful.

clue.text: Crossing yard quietly, eating nuts from Africa

indicators.note: the rearranged letters straddle the yard and quietly letters
nuts means crazy, so the letters of eating are scrambled

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone crossing a yard quietly, munching on nuts that came from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' rearranges EATING into EGTIAN, with YP put inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something from the land of the Nile and the pyramids, in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Discussion notes available here

definitions.meaning: a conversation or trading of views between people
a bureau where banknotes of one currency are swapped for another

explanation.definitionFit: A conversation trades words back and forth, and a bureau de change trades currencies, both a swapping.

clue.text: Issue around New Year causing malice

indicators.note: the issue word goes round the new letter

parts.note: to emit is to issue or send out

explanation.surface: A dispute at New Year leading to ill feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a noun, a dispute; it is the verb EMIT, round N, then Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility or ill will between parties amounts to spite and malice.

clue.text: Branded evil, good editor

parts.note: bad means evil

explanation.surface: An editor called evil and good at the same time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branded' suggests labelled as wicked; it is the definition, marked with an emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked with a badge or logo means carrying an emblem, as a branded product does.

clue.text: Lowers oneself to take in small objects

indicators.note: the condescending verb absorbs the small letter

parts.note: one who deigns condescends, lowering oneself

explanation.surface: Someone stooping to pick up small items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'objects' looks like things or a verb of protest; it is a plural noun, aims.
explanation.definitionFit: One's aims or intentions, as in having designs on something, are one's goals or objects.

clue.text: Male with a place excited about university admission

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the university letter
stirred up, so the letters of a place are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young man thrilled to win a place, getting into university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admission' looks like getting into university but means a confession; 'excited' turns A PLACE into EACLPA, around U.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase 'my fault' is an acknowledgement of guilt, a confession.

clue.text: All banks depleted — funds zero and below

indicators.note: the outer letters, the banks, of each of the next words are removed

explanation.surface: A grim financial report: every bank emptied, funds at zero and lower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' looks financial; here they are the edges of 'funds' and 'zero', leaving UND and ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Beneath or lower down in position is the meaning shared by these prepositions.

clue.text: Female animals cross in struggle with partners

indicators.note: the cross letter sits inside the struggle word

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
X is a cross shape
North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Angry female animals fighting it out alongside their mates.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the players sitting North and South form a partnership, so NS is partners.
explanation.definitionFit: These are female foxes, so the plural is a group of she-animals.

clue.text: Chosen most common Scrabble piece to pick up

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the word up reads it from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: the commonest Scrabble tile is the letter E, so this is E plus tile

explanation.surface: A player picks the commonest Scrabble tile from the bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pick up' reverses E TILE; the clue looks like an instruction to draw a tile.
explanation.definitionFit: A select few, the best picked out of many, are the chosen ones.

clue.text: Potato soup's starter, superior to dessert

indicators.note: in a down clue, superior means placed above the next piece
the first letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: pud is short for pudding, a dessert

explanation.surface: A menu verdict: a potato soup starter beats the dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior to' puts S above PUD; 'starter' plays on the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an informal, slangy word for a potato.

clue.text: Bore youngster heading off for bed

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: the first letter of the bed word is removed

parts.note: bed taken as written

explanation.surface: A tired child heading off to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tedious person; it is the past tense of bear, carried.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore as the past tense of bear means carried, and so does the verb for lugging something.

clue.text: Entering unprotected mine wielding club

indicators.note: without its outer cover, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: putting uses a putter, a golf club

explanation.surface: Breaking into an unguarded mine armed with a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a weapon; it is a golf club, the putter.
explanation.definitionFit: Keying in or typing data into a computer is entering it.

clue.text: Member of nobility in drugs den loaded with cash

indicators.note: loaded as in drunk or high, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An aristocrat found in a drugs den with a lot of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' looks like rich, matching the cash; it rearranges DRUGS DEN plus CASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman ruling a grand duchy, or a Russian imperial princess, is a high-ranking aristocrat.
